passage: Third summer camping at Lake Corrigan, and the locals still swear there's something huge living down there. Scientists have never proven there isn't, so honestly, I'm counting it as real. Bringing the good camera and the canoe this year. Wish me luck!
cue: Scientists have never proven there isn't, so honestly, I'm counting it as real.
explanation: Wes treats the lack of proof that there's no creature as a reason to believe there is one. Not having disproven something doesn't make it true.

whyNot.fal_burden_of_proof: Wes isn't demanding that anyone disprove him; he concludes it's real because no one has shown otherwise.

passage:
Priyanka: It's been a month since we switched to the four-day sprint cycle. Any feedback from your teams?
Byron: Nobody's complained, so I think it's safe to say everyone loves it.
Ji-ho: To be fair, the feedback form link was broken until yesterday.
cue: Nobody's complained, so I think it's safe to say everyone loves it.
explanation: Byron takes the absence of complaints as proof that everyone loves the change. Silence isn't approval, especially when, as Ji-ho notes, people couldn't easily give feedback.

whyNot.fal_burden_of_proof: Byron doesn't ask anyone to prove the team dislikes it; he reads a lack of complaints as evidence of approval.

title: Pebblestep Readers expanding next fall
passage: Dear families, we're excited to share that Pebblestep Readers will expand to every K-3 classroom next fall. Teachers enjoyed the training, and families have given the new books great marks. We haven't measured reading scores yet, but nothing so far suggests the program doesn't work, so we can be confident it's raising reading levels.
cue: nothing so far suggests the program doesn't work, so we can be confident it's raising reading levels
explanation: The positive feedback is real, but Alana admits reading scores haven't been measured, then concludes the program works because nothing shows it doesn't.

whyNot.fal_burden_of_proof: Alana doesn't ask families to disprove the program; she concludes it works simply because no evidence against it exists yet.

title: Parks director: new field infill is safe
passage: Asked about residents' questions over the rubber infill on the new Nettlefield Park sports fields, the parks director said no study has ever found the product harmful, so families can be confident it's safe. The infill, introduced by its manufacturer last year, has not yet been the subject of any published research.
cue: no study has ever found the product harmful, so families can be confident it's safe
explanation: The director treats "no study found harm" as proof of safety, but the last line shows no studies of this product exist at all. No harm has been found because nobody has looked.

whyNot.fal_burden_of_proof: The director doesn't demand that residents prove harm; he concludes the product is safe because harm hasn't been shown.

source: Councillor Yvette Marchand · Hollis Bay transportation committee
passage: I'll be the skeptic in the room. The protected bike lane on Dorsey Street has been open for three months, and so far there is no evidence it has reduced injuries. None. We were promised safer streets. If the data can't show it's working, then it isn't working, and I'll be moving to restore the parking.
cue: If the data can't show it's working, then it isn't working
explanation: Yvette sounds rigorous, but three months is likely too short to show any effect on injuries. She turns "not yet shown to work" into "shown not to work."

whyNot.fal_burden_of_proof: Asking supporters for evidence is fair; Yvette's error is concluding the lane fails because early data can't yet show an effect.

title: Five years. Zero breaches.
passage: Thriftwren has helped families track their spending since 2021. In five years, we've never had a single reported data breach, which tells you everything you need to know: your information is completely secure with us. Link your bank accounts in under two minutes and finally see where your money goes.
cue: we've never had a single reported data breach, which tells you everything you need to know
explanation: Thriftwren treats the absence of reported breaches as proof of complete security. A clean record is nice, but breaches can go undetected or unreported, so it can't show the app is secure.

whyNot.fal_burden_of_proof: Thriftwren doesn't ask anyone to prove the app insecure; it treats the absence of reported breaches as proof of security.

title: Inspection results
passage: Hi Daniel and Sofia, good news from this morning. The inspector spent two hours probing every accessible beam in the basement, crawlspace and attic and found no termite damage, droppings or mud tubes. If termites were active, those are exactly the signs she'd expect to see, so I'm comfortable saying there's no sign of an active infestation. Keisha
cue: If termites were active, those are exactly the signs she'd expect to see
explanation: The absence of evidence means something here: a thorough search looked for the specific signs termites leave, and Keisha keeps her conclusion appropriately modest.

whyNot.fal_appeal_to_ignorance: This isn't just "no one proved otherwise"; a careful search that would have found termite signs came up empty.

passage:
Ola: The leaked password belonged to an old admin account. Did anyone actually use it?
Kwame: I went through every authentication log since the account was created. Every login attempt is recorded, and there's not one from that account in two years.
Ola: Then it hasn't been used to get in. Let's disable it and close the ticket.
cue: Every login attempt is recorded, and there's not one from that account in two years
explanation: Ola's conclusion rests on a complete record: every login attempt is logged, so if the account had been used, Kwame's search would have found it.

whyNot.fal_appeal_to_ignorance: The missing evidence is meaningful because a full search of complete logs would have revealed any use of the account.
